data.name: Gorav
data.gender_notes: Gorav is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is born on a mountain or has a connection with mountains. In Hindu mythology, mountains are considered sacred and are believed to be the abode of gods. The name Gorav carries the meaning “Mountain-born” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gorav usually hope their child will grow to embody mountain-born and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Connection to divine mountain energies, stability, and strength.
data.etymology: Gorav belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mountain-born.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gorav total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

historical_references.reference: Gorakhnath was a 10th century Hindu saint and the founder of the Gorakhnath sect. He is also known as Gorakshanath and Goraveshvara. The Gorakhnath sect is a branch of the Nath tradition and is popular in North India. Gorakhnath is believed to have achieved perfection through hard penance and is known for his teachings on the importance of self-realization and the worship of Shiva.
historical_references.context: Founder of the Gorakhnath sect, a branch of the Nath tradition in North India, and is revered for his teachings on self-realization and the worship of Shiva.

historical_references.reference: Gorakshas were a group of Hindu guards who protected Lord Rama during his exile in the forest. They were warriors and ascetics who wore the skin of a tiger or a panther as armor. They are mentioned in the Indian epic Ramayana, and their leader was Jambavan, the king of the bears. Gorakshas are believed to be the protectors of Rama and his brother Lakshmana, and they played a significant role in helping Rama regain his kingdom and defeat the demon king Ravana.
historical_references.context: Group of Hindu guards who protected Lord Rama during his exile and are mentioned in the Indian epic Ramayana. Gorakshas are believed to be the protectors of Rama and his brother Lakshmana.
